items.title: Influencers pushed mercury-laced cream; a 17-year-old Keralam girl paid with her kidneys
items.summary: A 17-year-old girl in Malappuram is recovering from a serious kidney disorder after using Ftune, a fairness cream promoted by multiple Instagram influencers. Doctors at a private hospital, who tested the product found that the cream contained 12,500 parts per million (1.25 per cent) of mercury, more than 12,000 times the 1 ppm limit set for most cosmetics in India. Mercury is a toxic heavy metal, and decades of research have warned against its use in cosmetics. The usage of Skin Lightening Products (SLPs) have often been linked to prejudice against people with darker skin by centuries of colonialism, white supremacy and classism, and a multi-crore fairness industry thrives on it. The plight of the teenager has now prompted the Kerala State Commission for Protection of Child Rights to register a suo motu case. The teenager developed a severe kidney disorder, membranous nephropathy, in which immune deposits thicken the filtering walls of the kidneys, caused by mercury poisoning linked to the cream.
